meta.title: Validation gates
meta.purpose: A strategy is admitted to the leaderboard only if it clears every HARD gate. Gates exist to make luck expensive. Each gate states its criterion, the evidence it needs, and what happens when it fails.
meta.design_principle: Ordered by cost: the cheapest disqualifiers run first, so a bad idea is killed before anyone spends money on it.

gates.name: Data sufficiency
gates.criterion: A complete, timestamped record of the price available at decision time and the closing price, for every bet. No look-ahead: no field may be populated from a source published after the decision timestamp.
gates.needs: Odds archive with snapshot times; games logs; leg-level outcomes for props
gates.failure: Strategy cannot be scored at all. State: BLOCKED, reason recorded.
gates.why: Without this there is nothing to measure. It is gate zero because every later gate silently assumes it.

gates.name: Pre-registered sample size
gates.criterion: n >= required_n for the smallest edge the strategy claims to detect, with n fixed BEFORE evaluation.
gates.numbers: 2.0pp edge over a 52.4% break-even needs 4,887 graded bets (win/loss test) or 19,623 (ROI test) at 80% power.
gates.failure: Result is reported as 'insufficient evidence', never as 'promising'.
gates.why: Fixes the sample by design instead of stopping when the chart looks good — the most common source of false discovery in small-sample betting projects.

gates.name: Statistical significance with multiplicity
gates.criterion: t-statistic on mean CLV >= the threshold implied by Bonferroni over the logged trial count (t >= 1.96 with one trial; t >= 3.31 with 100 trials).
gates.failure: Not admitted. The trial count must be honest or the gate is void.
gates.why: Searching many ideas guarantees apparent winners. The correction is the price of the search.
gates.numbers: t >= 1.96 with one trial; t >= 3.48 with 100 logged trials; t >= 3.89 with 500. See the multiplicity table below, which is computed, not quoted.

gates.name: Locked holdout
gates.criterion: >= 30% of the available seasons are never used for design, and are evaluated exactly once.
gates.needs: Season-level split recorded before model work
gates.failure: Not admitted; the holdout cannot be reused for that strategy.
gates.why: A holdout that has been looked at twice is a training set.

gates.name: Walk-forward only
gates.criterion: Every parameter used at time t is estimated only from data strictly before t. No retrospective parameter selection.
gates.why: This is the difference between a backtest and a story.

gates.name: Deflated Sharpe
gates.criterion: Deflated Sharpe ratio (Bailey & Lopez de Prado) > 0.95 given the trial count.
gates.numbers: At n=500 observations and a single trial, the bar is an observed Sharpe of about 0.10; with 50 logged trials it rises to about 0.18. Searching raises the bar faster than it raises the best result, which is the whole point of the gate.
gates.why: Sharpe alone rewards search. The deflation charges for it.

gates.name: Closing-line value positive
gates.criterion: Mean CLV > 0 with the G2 confidence requirement.
gates.failure: Not admitted, even if realised ROI is positive.
gates.why: Beating the close is the best available evidence of skill per bet, and it is far less noisy than win/loss. A profitable run without positive CLV is variance, not edge.

gates.name: Segment stability
gates.criterion: The sign of the edge agrees in >= 3 of 4 segments: home/away, favourite/underdog, first/second half of season, conference.
gates.failure: Not admitted; log which segment reversed.
gates.why: An edge that only exists in one slice is usually a label artefact.

gates.name: Bootstrap lower bound
gates.criterion: 10,000-resample bootstrap 95% CI lower bound on mean edge > 0.
gates.why: Removes reliance on a normal approximation that per-bet returns violate badly.

gates.name: Correlation integrity
gates.criterion: Joint probability is priced from estimated pairwise rho per market cluster, not from independence. rho must be estimated on >= 2 seasons and reported per cluster.
gates.failure: Parlay strategies are BLOCKED (not merely unscored).
gates.why: Independence pricing of correlated legs manufactures edge out of nothing, and it fails in the direction that costs the most money.

gates.name: Participation gating (props)
gates.criterion: A prop is only eligible if the player's availability is resolved (official designation, then inactive list), and the usage assumption is validated against the player's own recent workload.
gates.needs: Official designations + inactive list + snap/usage data
gates.why: A prop bet on a player who does not take the field is not a bad prediction, it is a different bet.

gates.name: Capacity
gates.criterion: Intended stake <= 5% of the typical available limit in that market; edge survives at the achievable price, not just the best price.
gates.failure: Downgraded to 'research only'; may not receive reward allocation.
gates.why: An edge you cannot get filled at is a spreadsheet artefact.

gates.name: Governance
gates.criterion: Versioned rule text, immutable bet log, pre-registration commit hash, and a recorded trial count. No rule may change inside an evaluation window.
gates.needs: Git commit before first graded bet
gates.why: Without an audit trail, every other gate is self-reported.

reward_tiers.meaning: Idea exists; nothing has been demonstrated.

reward_tiers.reward: research priority only (compute + data access, no money)
reward_tiers.meaning: Runnable and honest, not yet demonstrably skilful.

reward_tiers.reward: small live allocation, capped at 1/4 Kelly
reward_tiers.meaning: Beats the close and is stable across segments.

reward_tiers.reward: largest allocation, capped; still subject to drawdown stop
reward_tiers.meaning: Skill-based, sized, and able to absorb money.

hard_rule: A strategy that fails ANY hard gate receives no reward, regardless of realised profit. This is the mechanism that stops the leaderboard from paying for luck.
